parts.label: Part 1
parts.article:
Part one. You will hear a woman phoning a hotel manager to inquire about holding a wedding ceremony. First, you have some time to look at questions one to five.

Now listen carefully and answer questions one to five.

Hello, Clarence House.

Oh, hello. Um, I'm getting married next year, and I understand you're licensed to hold weddings at the hotel.

Yes, we are. Can I ask what date you were thinking of?

Either the first or the seventh of June.

Right. Let me see.

Oh, I'm afraid we already have a booking for the seventh, but we still have availability on June the first.

That would be fine.

Huh. So how many guests are you going to be inviting?

About eighty.

So for that number, we'd recommend the Oxford Suite. I don't know if you've been to the hotel.

Yes. In fact, I went to a wedding there a few years ago, and I was really impressed.

Very good.

I think we were in the Oxford Suite then. Um, the room where we were eating had big windows with really good views. You could see right across the city. [laughs]

[laughs] That's it. And you'd have exclusive access to the garden. It'll be at its best in June.

So we could have the photos there?

Sure. In fact, you can even have the ceremony there if you want. It makes a lovely background.

Oh, I hadn't thought of that. Yes, that's certainly an idea.

And is there somewhere for dancing?

Yes. There's plenty of space in the middle of the dining room.

Oh, yeah, I remember now.

So just to give you an idea, would you like me to tell you about our special wedding package?

Sure.

Right. So for eighty guests, you'd have the exclusive use of the Oxford Suite, as I said, and then a meal. So that would be in the dining room, and that would be a sit-down meal with three courses.

And how is the room arranged? I seem to remember you have round tables.

That's right. Most people prefer them to long tables.

Long tables aren't really very friendly, are they? [laughs] And what about decorations on the tables?

They're included in the package. And we have white linen tablecloths and white chair covers. And we also include an individually designed menu specially printed for you. It's something that people can take away to remember the occasion. That's something we've just started doing this year.

Oh, right.

Before you hear the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at questions six to ten.

Now listen and answer questions six to ten.

And then towards the end of the evening, when everyone's beginning to run out of energy, we bring in a buffet. Nothing too complicated, just a selection of sandwiches together with tea or coffee. That's always very popular.

Hmm. Right. And we'll want some music. Is that included in the package?

No, but we could probably get you a DJ, or we know of a very good band if you'd prefer that.

Yes, that'd be better, actually. Something to get everyone on their feet. [laughs] Good. So apart from the music, you said that's an all-inclusive package. So how much does that package come to?

Five thousand nine hundred and ninety-five pounds.

That's a bit more than the package they quoted for me at the Stanley Hotel. Theirs was four thousand five hundred pounds.

Yes, but I think if you look at what you're getting for the money, you'll find we're the best value. And it is a big day after all.

Yes, you're probably right.

Oh, and I nearly forgot. I'm looking for someone who can make me a really special cake. Can you suggest one?

Certainly. There's a new company that we've started using. They're very good. In fact, our wedding coordinator will be able to give you all sorts of advice. We can offer you a free consultation and a tour of the venue.

Yes. Well, I'd definitely be interested.

Right. Well, the coordinator's name is Sarah Izard. That's I-Z-A-R-D.

Now, when would you like to meet her? She's available from nine to five most weekdays or later if that's more convenient.

Uh, I'm free on the twelfth of October, in the morning sometime, or the fifteenth of October.

That would be better, thanks. Should we say eleven thirty?

Fine.

And can I just take your name and a contact number?

Sure. It's Debbie.

That is the end of part one. You now have one minute to check your answers to part one.

analyses.content: 录音中明确提到吃饭的房间窗户很大、视野很好，可以直接看穿整个城市（see right across the city）。
Um, the room where we were eating had big windows with really good views. You could see right across the city.
你可能会听到“windows”或“views”，但题目问的是“view of the...”（……的景色），结合介词搭配和上下文可知看的是“city”。
And you'd have exclusive access to the garden. It'll be at its best in June. / So we could have the photos there? / Sure. In fact, you can even have the ceremony there if you want.
你可能会听到后文的“ceremony”，但题目里已经印了ceremony，结合空前的“for”可知你需要填的是另一个在花园进行的活动“photos”。
女方主动提问是否可以在花园拍照（have the photos there），男方立刻给予了肯定的回答。
And how is the room arranged? I seem to remember you have round tables. / That's right. Most people prefer them to long tables.
你可能会听到男方后面提到的“long tables”，但这只是用来对比衬托的干扰项，实际采用的是大多数人偏爱的“round”桌子。
女方询问房间布置时，回忆说之前用的是圆桌（round tables），男方紧接着用“That's right”确认了这一点。
[laughs] And what about decorations on the tables? / They're included in the package.
答案给得非常直白，但你可能会因为录音里的“on the tables”和题目里的“table ___”发生了介词结构到名词修饰的转换，导致没跟上，注意抓取核心名词即可。
女方直接提问桌子上的装饰品（decorations on the tables）怎么算，男方回答说它们已经包含在套餐内（included in the package）。
And we also include an individually designed menu specially printed for you. It's something that people can take away to remember the occasion.
你可能会被“individually designed”这长串修饰词干扰，但它和题干的“personalised”是完美替换，紧跟其后的核心名词“menu”才是真正的答案。
男方介绍套餐内容时，提到会提供一份专门为你打印的、独立设计的菜单（individually designed menu specially printed for you）。
男方介绍晚宴结束前的自助餐时，说明食物不复杂，只提供精选的三明治（a selection of sandwiches）配茶或咖啡。

And then towards the end of the evening, when everyone's beginning to run out of energy, we bring in a buffet. Nothing too complicated, just a selection of sandwiches together with tea or coffee. That's always very popular.
你可能会听到“tea or coffee”，但这对应了题目已经印好的“hot drinks”；前面的“a selection of”完美替换了题目里的“a choice of”，所以顺位填“sandwiches”。

So how much does that package come to? / Five thousand nine hundred and ninety-five pounds. / That's a bit more than the package they quoted for me at the Stanley Hotel. Theirs was four thousand five hundred pounds.
你极其容易被女方随后抱怨的另一家酒店（Stanley Hotel）的报价“4500（four thousand five hundred）”干扰，注意认准提问主体Clarence House的报价。
女方询问全包套餐的总价，男方直截了当地回答是五千九百九十五英镑（Five thousand nine hundred and ninety-five）。
Oh, and I nearly forgot. I'm looking for someone who can make me a really special cake. Can you suggest one? / Certainly. There's a new company that we've started using.
这里的语序是答案倒置，你可能会把所有注意力都放在等题目里的“new company”出现，从而错过了前面女方主动提出的核心诉求词“cake”。
女方说想找人做一个特别的蛋糕（special cake）并询问推荐，男方回答说正好有一家刚开始合作的“新公司”可以做。
Well, the coordinator's name is Sarah Izard. That's I-Z-A-R-D.
这是一道单纯的字母拼写题，听到了就开始写，不要因为思考前文或者发音口音问题导致字母跟丢。
男方直接报出了婚礼协调员的名字Sarah，并明确给出了姓氏的拼写 I-Z-A-R-D。
Uh, I'm free on the twelfth of October in the morning sometime, or the fifteenth of October. / That would be better, thanks. Should we say eleven thirty? / Fine.
典型的二选一陷阱，你很容易把最先听到的“twelfth of October（12日）”当成答案，必须听完整段对话看双方最终确认（agree on）的是哪一个。
女方给了两个见面的时间选项（10月12日或10月15日），男方表示后面那个（That would be better）更好，敲定了15日。
